arguments.arg1_rdi: out status struct (caller-provided). The function returns this pointer in rax. Status layout: bytes 0..5 plus a pointer at +8 (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8). The byte at +0 gates the replay and cache paths.
arguments.arg2_rsi: context struct (kept in r14 on the driver paths). Fields used: +0 (its first field points at an object whose +0x30 field is the unknown-type log call's logger argument), +0xa0 (head of the error-callback link chain), +0x110 (mutex object for the cache lookup/insert), +0x148 (directory string pair {pointer, length} used by both filename builders), +0xd8/+0xe0/+0xe8/+0xf0/+0xf8 (replay cache table, see cache_table), +0x30 is NOT read on the driver paths (the +0x30 read belongs to the object at (context)).
arguments.arg3_edx: file type, compared UNSIGNED. Values 0 and 1 take the driver paths; any other value (edx > 1 unsigned) takes the unknown-type path, which logs and returns a code-3 status without touching the cache or the replay step.
arguments.arg4_rcx: log number (u64). It is the cache-table key, the filename number formatted as %06llu, and the replay step's fourth argument (passed unchanged as its reader-constructor r9).
arguments.arg5_r8: out-pointer slot (u64). Zeroed at entry. The cache-hit path writes the cached value into it; the replay step writes into it on the miss paths (see the replay-step packet); the cache-insert path reads it back and inserts only when it is nonzero.

cache_insert.condition: reached only from the type-0 post-replay path when the replay status byte 0 is 0. The mutex at context+0x110 is re-locked first (call 0x5334c00 at 0x520ce60); it is unlocked at 0x520cf17 after the insert decision.
cache_insert.existing_key: the segment walk finds the key: the fresh 0x18-byte node is freed with operator delete (size 0x18, call at 0x520cf12), the table is unchanged, and control returns to the propagate step. The walk's (before-node)==0 sub-arm jumps to the insert path instead, but it cannot fire from a consistent walk (the before-node's next is the matched node itself), so it is recorded as observed, not as a live path.
cache_insert.fresh_node: operator new 0x18 bytes (call at 0x520ce6e). Layout: next +0 = 0, key +8 = log number, value +16 = the out-slot value read at entry to this path.
cache_insert.insert_rules: bucket = key mod bucket count (count at +0xe0). Empty bucket: the new node becomes the head (context+0xe8), the old head (if any) keeps its bucket entry repointed at the new node, and this bucket's entry is set to the sentinel address (context+0xe8). Nonempty bucket: the new node is inserted after the before-node (before-node next = new node, new node next = old first node). Element count at +0xf0 increases by 1 on either rule.
cache_insert.rehash: _M_need_rehash is called with (policy at context+0xf8, bucket count at +0xe0, element count at +0xf0, 1); the policy's next-resize field (context+0x100) is saved to a stack slot first. On need, the rehash auxiliary 0x5160ad0 is called with (table at context+0xd8, the new count returned by _M_need_rehash, the saved-next-resize slot pointer), and the bucket is recomputed mod the new count. The policy float value itself is not pinned.
cache_insert.status_after: the replay status byte is forced to 0 before propagation (movb $0 at 0x520ccd6), on both the insert and the skip (slot was zero) sub-paths.

cache_lookup.bucketed_walk: taken when element count at +0xf0 is nonzero. Bucket = key mod bucket count at +0xe0. Walk from the bucket entry's node: compare each node's key at +8 with the log number; on match, the value at +16 is the hit. The walk stops (miss) at chain end or at the first node whose key hashes to a different bucket. A bucket entry of 0 is an immediate miss.
cache_lookup.found_path: the cached value is stored into the out-pointer slot, the out status is zeroed (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8), the mutex is unlocked (call 0x5334cc0 at 0x520c89c), and the function returns. The replay step is never called on this path.
cache_lookup.linear_walk: taken when element count at +0xf0 is zero. Walk from the head at +0xe8 following next at +0, comparing key at +8; a null head is an immediate miss. (In a consistent table the head is null when the count is zero, so this walk exits at once.)
cache_lookup.locking: the mutex at context+0x110 is locked first (call 0x5334c00 at 0x520c840). On a miss it is unlocked (call 0x5334cc0 at 0x520ca23) BEFORE the filename is built, so the replay step runs without the lock.
cache_lookup.node: stride 0x18 in the bucket chains: next +0, key +8, value +16.

callers.note: census by numpy-vectorized .text e8 scan, e9 scan, and whole-file qword scan. The caller loops over elements (stride 0x20) with a predicate call 0x529f350 and a stack flag check, then calls the driver with (out status at stack +0x18, context at stack +0x08, file type from stack +0x04, log number from stack +0x58, out-pointer slot at stack +0x60). The caller's own choice of file-type values is census only; the driver pins both type arms itself.

digit_table.assembled: the 200-byte sequence of two-character decimal pairs "00".."99" in order (verified by simulating the 13 chunk copies, including the unaligned tail store, in verify.py).
digit_table.copy: twelve aligned 16-byte copies to the stack table (pairs 00..95), then one unaligned 16-byte store at table offset 185 covering the tail (second character of pair 92 plus pairs 93..99 plus a NUL). The loop indexes table[2*remainder] and table[2*remainder+1].
digit_table.note: the model implements decimal conversion arithmetically, not via the table; the tests prove identical outputs, including values exercising every pair index band.

error_chain.all_match: if all 10 links match, the final link's +0xe8 target is called (call *0xe8(%rax)).
error_chain.args: the chain function is called with (status scratch pointer, filename string object pointer): rdi = the stack address of the replay status scratch (rsp+0x40), rdx = the stack address of the filename string object (rsp+0x70 slot). The call may rewrite the scratch status byte, which decides the next step.
error_chain.links: the chain head is the object at context+0xa0. Links advance through +0x48. Each link's identity field at +0xe8 is compared against the runtime value at 0x5778258. Path A (type 0) examines 10 links (the head plus 9 advances); path B (type 1) examines 10 links the same way.
error_chain.meaning: inference only: the chain reads as a list of callback/listener objects whose identity is checked before invocation. The objects' types, the virtual method's semantics, and the global at 0x5778258 are NOT pinned; see unknowns.
error_chain.mismatch: on the first identity mismatch, that link's +0xe8 target is called directly (call *%rax on the even steps, call *%rcx on the odd steps, both with the same two arguments) and the walk stops.

filename_builders.format: %06llu.%s at 0x1e8058, rendered with (log number, "log" at 0x202ac1): six-digit zero-padded decimal, longer numbers untruncated, plus ".log".
filename_builders.runtime_component: the type-0 builder appends one further path component from a runtime-set (pointer, length) pair read from 0x578df20/0x578df28 (beyond the file-backed data segment, so its content is NOT pinned from the binary). Its role is exactly one extra path component between the directory and the file name.
filename_builders.type0: helper 0x529d060 (out string, directory pair at context+0x148, log number): out = directory + "/" + runtime component + "/" + "%06llu.log" % log number. Implemented by appending directory, separator, and the runtime component, then delegating to 0x529c540 for the final component.
filename_builders.type1: helper 0x529ca20 (out string, directory pair at context+0x148, log number) delegates to 0x529c540 (out string, directory pair, log number, "log"): out = directory + "/" + "%06llu.log" % log number.
filename_builders.type1_note: 0x529c540 appends the directory bytes, then "/", then the snprintf result into the out string (length-overflow arms throw length_error past 0x3fffffffffffffff; recorded, not modeled as output).

not_claimed: the error-chain objects' types and the +0xe8 method's semantics
the content of the runtime path component at 0x578df20/0x578df28
the identity of the logger object behind (context)+0x30
the detail builder's internals beyond its (out, code, subcode, message) contract
the cache policy float value at context+0xf8
LSDA/exception-pad mapping: landing stubs at 0x520d299..0x520d31d jump into the 0x520c054..0x520c120 region; the mapping is not pinned
behavior of the caller beyond its call setup
internals of the replay step, filename helpers, lock/unlock wrappers, and rehash auxiliary beyond their pinned contracts

post_replay_type0.byte0_nonzero: the error chain runs (see error_chain). Afterwards the scratch status byte 0 is re-read: if it is 1, the out status is zeroed (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8), the buffers are freed, and the function returns; otherwise the saved replay status is propagated to out (see status_copy).
post_replay_type0.byte0_zero: the cache-insert path runs (see cache_insert), then the saved replay status is propagated to out.
post_replay_type0.scratch_copy: immediately after the replay call, the scratch status bytes are saved: byte 0 to a stack slot, bytes 1..5 to stack slots, and the pointer field to a stack slot; the scratch u32/u16 fields are then zeroed. The saved bytes (not the scratch) are what propagation writes to out, except the byte-1 zeroing arm, which zeroes out entirely.

post_replay_type1.byte0_nonzero: the error chain runs (same 10-link shape). Afterwards the scratch status byte 0 is re-read: if it is nonzero, the filename is rebuilt with the TYPE-0 builder and the replay step runs again, followed by the full type-0 post-replay sequence (cache insert on byte 0, error chain on nonzero, byte-1 zeroing); if it is zero, the saved replay status is propagated to out.
post_replay_type1.byte0_zero: the saved replay status is propagated to out directly (no cache insert on this path).

replay_calls.note: both calls target the replay step 0x520ad30 (see its packet). The scratch status at rsp+0x40 is the step's out argument; the filename string object at the rsp+0x70 slot is its filename argument; the log number is its fourth argument; the out-pointer slot (r12) is its fifth argument.
replay_calls.type0_site: 0x520ca74, after the filename is built by 0x529d060 at 0x520ca56.
replay_calls.type1_site: 0x520cd74, after the filename is built by 0x529ca20 at 0x520cd56.

status_copy.layout: out status = 6 bytes (bytes 0..5) plus a pointer at +8. Path A copies byte 0 from its saved slot and bytes 1..5 from their saved slots in order; path B copies bytes 0..1 as one u16, byte 2 singly, bytes 3..4 as one u16, and byte 5 singly. Both write the same six bytes and the same pointer; the two paths differ only in copy order (compiler scheduling).
status_copy.zero_status: u32 at +0 = 0, u16 at +4 = 0, pointer at +8 = 0. Used on the cache-hit path and on the type-0 byte-1 arm.

unknown_type.condition: file type edx > 1, compared UNSIGNED (jbe at 0x520c15a takes the driver paths for 0 and 1).
unknown_type.decimal: the value is formatted as a SIGNED decimal: sign = edx >> 31, magnitude = edx when the sign is 0, -edx when the sign is 1 (INT_MIN keeps magnitude 0x80000000, whose digits are 2147483648, so the rendered text is still the signed value). Digit counts by magnitude: <=9: 1, <=99: 2, <=999: 3, <=9999: 4, <=99999: 5, <=999999: 6, <=9999999: 7, <=99999999: 8, <=999999999: 9, else 10. Digits are produced least-significant-pair first with imul 0x51eb851f / shr 0x25 (division by 100) against the digit-pair table (see digit_table). A leading '-' is written when the sign is 1.
unknown_type.detail: detail builder 0x542f040 (out status, code 3, subcode 0, message string, scratch, 0). The message is the 20-byte prefix "File Type Not Known " (0x1df471, trailing space included) prepended to the decimal via _M_replace at 0x520c5ac (position 0, count 0, 20 bytes). Code 3 renders as "Not implemented: " under the status formatter (see its packet), so the rendered status text is "Not implemented: File Type Not Known <decimal>"; that rendering is derived, not observed in this window.
unknown_type.effect: returns the code-3 status in out. The cache is never locked, the replay step is never called, and the out-pointer slot stays 0.
unknown_type.log: variadic log dispatcher 0x522ea30 (level argument 3, logger argument = (context)+0x30, format "[%s:381] [WalManger] Unknown file type %s" at 0x7d6168, file "db/wal_manager.cc" at 0x1f989e, decimal string). Rendered line, with the binary's verbatim "WalManger" spelling: "[db/wal_manager.cc:381] [WalManger] Unknown file type <decimal>". The log uses a separately built copy of the decimal string (no prefix).
unknown_type.log_string_note: the log call's first format argument is the file string itself (rcx = 0x1f989e) and the second is the decimal string (r8); the "381" is literal in the format.

unknowns: the error-chain objects' types and the +0xe8 method's semantics, and the meaning of the global at 0x5778258
the content of the runtime path component at 0x578df20/0x578df28
the identity of the logger object behind (context)+0x30
the cache policy float value at context+0xf8 (only its call contract is pinned)

window.canary: fs:0x28 saved at rsp+0x168, checked before return (failure calls __stack_chk_fail at 0x520d294)
window.landing_stubs: 0x520d299..0x520d31d (endbr64 stubs jumping into the 0x520c054..0x520c120 region; LSDA mapping not claimed)

cache_table.layout: buckets pointer +0xd8, bucket count +0xe0, head (before-begin next) +0xe8, element count +0xf0, policy +0xf8 (load-factor float at +0xf8, next-resize at +0x100).
cache_table.insertion_rule: Nonempty bucket: the new node is inserted after the bucket ENTRY node (the before-node recorded in the entry), not after the last node of the segment; the walk only detects duplicates. Empty bucket: prepend to head with the old-head repoint and the entry set to the sentinel (see cache_insert).
